findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top-ranked convergence gene: it is up in UC biopsies (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]) and has strong Open Targets genetic support ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]). It is tractable (small molecule: advanced clinical) with reparixin at PHASE_3 and several other antagonists at PHASE_2 (none is a UC-approved drug).

Reactome places CXCR2 in neutrophil degranulation, chemokine receptors binding chemokines and G alpha(i) signalling. STRING high-confidence partners are the ELR+ chemokines CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL2, CXCL6, CXCL3 plus PPBP and CXCR1, defining a neutrophil-recruitment axis.

CXCR1 is the second-ranked gene, up in biopsies ([gene=CXCR1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.769]) with genetic and drug support shared with CXCR2 (reparixin PHASE_3, ladarixin, navarixin, SX-682 at PHASE_2). It is probably co-targeted with CXCR2 by the same antagonists.

CXCL8 is strongly up ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.704]) and replicates in five cohorts, but it has no Open Targets genetic association signal (genetics component zero in the ranking); its drugs are ABX-IL8 and adakitug, both PHASE_2. Expression-led and literature-led, not genetically supported.

IL23R has very strong genetic association ([gene=IL23R; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.9411]) but barely changes in biopsies ([gene=IL23R; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-0.292]), so it ranks well below the top fifty of the target profile and is not in the convergence top. A genetically supported gene that expression does not capture (IL23 pathway drugs act upstream via IL12B/IL23A).

CHI3L1 is among the most up-regulated genes ([gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.714]) and replicates in five cohorts, but it has no known drug and no genetic association; it is a biomarker candidate rather than a drug target. The same expression-only, undrugged profile applies to DUOX2, AQP9, S100A8/S100A9, LCN2 and CXCL1.

IDO1 is strongly induced ([gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445]) with no genetic association; Open Targets lists epacadostat (max stage APPROVAL as returned) and linrodostat (PHASE_3), both from other indications, so repurposing is a hypothesis only.

OSMR combines up-regulation ([gene=OSMR; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.042]) with Open Targets genetic support and an antibody (vixarelimab, PHASE_2, antibody tractability advanced clinical); its Reactome pathway is IL-6-type cytokine receptor ligand interactions.

JAK2 has a high Open Targets UC score ([gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) but only a modest biopsy change ([gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]); drugs listed (e.g. fedratinib, approval) are in other indications.

FCGR2A has strong genetic association ([gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.87]) with a small expression change and no listed drug; the signal likely reflects infiltrating myeloid cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in biopsies ([gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.887]) and has approved antibodies from oncology (e.g. atezolizumab, PHASE_4); an agonist-direction hypothesis in UC is untested here, since existing drugs block the pathway.

MMP1 is strongly up ([gene=MMP1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.661]) without genetic support; marimastat and doxycycline are listed but are broad MMP inhibitors, so MMP1, MMP3, MMP7 and MMP10 are better read as tissue-damage biomarkers.

caveats: Established UC targets TNF and JAK1 are not in the stored convergence, target or biomarker rankings, so the ranking favours up-regulated genes over drug targets whose expression is unchanged.
Drug stages are from Open Targets in any indication; none of the CXCR2 or IDO1 drugs is shown to be approved for UC.
Only CXCR2, OSMR and CD274 target profiles were queried directly; other drug and tractability details come from the convergence ranking records.
Open Targets genetic association was zero or absent for most of the strongest expression-led genes, which says nothing about causality.
